title: Title: Adaptive Phase-Coherence Synchronization for Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Quantum algorithms rely heavily on precise phase-coherence, a delicate phenomenon crucial for computation. Current synchronization protocols often employ fixed parameters, limiting the algorithm's performance. This paper investigates and presents an adaptive phase-coherence synchronization protocol, designed to dynamically adjust synchronization parameters based on the evolving phase-coherence dynamics of quantum systems. We propose a novel approach that leverages a feedback mechanism to optimize synchronization fidelity, addressing limitations of existing methods and opening avenues for enhanced quantum algorithm execution. The core mechanism involves a self-regulating algorithm that continually monitors the quantum state and adjusts synchronization parameters to maintain optimal phase-coherence. This adaptability will significantly improve the fidelity of quantum algorithms, offering a more robust and efficient solution.

title: Optimizing Referee Assignments with Fuzzy Evaluation and Particle Swarm Intelligence
abstract: Referee assignment is a recurring challenge in a wide range of settings—from assigning officials to sports matches to allocating reviewers for academic conferences. These scenarios often involve complex constraints, such as assigning multiple referees to a single activity or allowing referees to evaluate multiple tasks. In this study, we address a generalized version of the referee assignment problem, focusing on the case where each activity is matched with exactly one referee. To evaluate the suitability of assignments, we leverage rating scores across multiple dimensions for both referees and activities. These scores are incorporated into fuzzy membership functions that quantify assignment quality. We propose a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm that uses these fuzzy-based evaluations to guide the search for optimal assignments. Synthetic datasets with varying levels of data dispersion—generated from uniform distributions with equal means but different variances—are used to test the algorithm. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PSO approach is not only computationally efficient but also robust across different variance scenarios. This method offers a flexible and adaptable solution for a broad class of referee-assignment problems.

title: Multi-USVs Collaborative Water Pollution Traceability and Source Localization Using an Improved Wolf Pack Algorithm
abstract: With the increasing frequency of water pollution incidents due to urbanization and industrialization, this paper proposes an Improved Wolf Pack Algorithm (IWPA) for coordinating multiple Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs) to achieve rapid river pollution traceability. The IWPA incorporates a dynamic step adjustment mechanism and a dynamic population adjustment strategy to overcome the limitations of the fixed step factor and random repositioning in the standard Wolf Pack Algorithm (WPA). These enhancements prevent the algorithm from converging on local optima and improve the overall traceability efficiency of the multi-USV formation. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of IWPA. Under conditions of a 1500 g/s source emission rate, a 3 m/s longitudinal flow velocity, and using only 5 USVs, IWPA achieves a success rate of 97.3% and an average localization error of 0.41 m. These results represent improvements of 15.9% in success rate and 71.3% in error reduction compared to the standard WPA. Laboratory-based water pollution traceability tests further confirm the method’s effectiveness, with a success rate of 80%, validating its practical localization capability.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Frameworks for Data Analysis
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) frameworks present a new paradigm for data analysis that uses the parallelism and entanglement of quantum computing to facilitate efficient learning. In this paper we introduce a new robust, scalable and hybrid QML framework to address shortcomings of existing models, such as sensitivity to noise, scalability, and interpretability. By combining quantum kernel methods, variational circuits, and hybrid training routines, the framework offers practical data applications in finance, healthcare and cybersecurity. Its scalability and versatility are supported by benchmarks over simulators and true quantum hardware. This work paves the way for future-proof modular quantum-enhanced data analytics systems.

title: Threshold Choice, Not Sample Size, Bounds Trustless Verification of Nondeterministic Compound AI Workflows
abstract: Compound AI pipelines chain LLM calls, retrievers, and tools and are nondeterministic: sampling, model updates, and volatile tool responses make one input yield different outputs across runs. Such pipelines increasingly run across edge, cloud, and orbital nodes owned by no single party, whose optimizations discard intermediate results before inspection. Verifying reproduction there means tolerating nondeterministic outputs, a node that may not report honestly, and intermittent access to any shared record; existing work addresses at most two at once. We give a protocol covering all three: it commits digests of each stage's inputs, outputs, and context under a policy digest pinning the metric and threshold, anchors them without trusting the executing node, defers under partition, and decides a challenge on the median of $k$ re-executions, with no quorum. Where that procedure breaks is the main result. On a synthetic HotpotQA pipeline a calibrated fixed threshold accepts 44 of 45 honest reproductions and rejects 104 of 105 divergent pairs, yet lets same-input fabrication through in 27 of 29 trials at k=5, more samples being no help since sampling sharpens an estimate without moving it. Holding that metric and this pipeline's re-execution spread fixed, the binding constraint is the threshold rather than the sample size: one derived per execution detects 19 of 29 where the best constant matched to the same zero honest rejections reaches 9, rejects no honest commitment at k=5 though 3 of 15 at k=3, and catches 11 of 15 of an attacker built against it, which has to aim at a target drawn only after its commitment exists. That rule is measured rather than deployed.

title: SGD in Multiclass Logistic Regression: Sequential Learning and Scaling Laws
abstract: We study the training dynamics of multiclass logistic regression on high-dimensional Gaussian mixture models with a large number of classes and establish precise scaling laws governing the cross-entropy risk under gradient-based optimization. We show that learning proceeds sequentially across classes, from most to least frequent. When the class priors follow a power law distribution, the risk dynamics decompose into three phases: an initial plateau until the first class is learned, a power-law decay regime during which sequential learning occurs, and a final convergence regime. We then analyze how model capacity interacts with optimization under a fixed compute budget. When the effective dimension is restricted via projection onto leading principal components, the risk decomposes into a capacity term (a power law in the retained dimension) and an optimization term (a power law in training time). Optimizing this tradeoff yields a compute-optimal scaling law for logistic regression, with explicit prescriptions for model size and training time as functions of compute. These results extend theoretical scaling laws from linear regression to multiclass classification, while connecting to empirical scaling laws observed in large-scale neural networks.

title: CEDAR: Error-Bounded Residual Routing for Efficient Long-Context Attention
abstract: Post-hoc sparse attention accelerates long-context prefill by routing each query to a small set of token-level interactions. Hard selection, however, assigns zero probability to every omitted chunk: a routing miss cannot be recovered, and a fixed expansion budget spends the same work on easy and ambiguous queries. We introduce Coarse-to-fine Error-aware Dynamic Attention Routing (CEDAR), a coarse-to-fine method that keeps the language model frozen while preserving global coverage. Each semantic chunk contributes a cheap key--value summary to a residual attention path; chunks with high estimated approximation error are then expanded to exact token attention. Exact and summarized contributions are combined in a single softmax normalization, so refinement replaces, rather than duplicates, coarse evidence. We derive an output-error bound governed by within-chunk key/value dispersion and use it to allocate a variable refinement budget. A controlled clustered-attention study shows that residual summaries reduce reconstruction error by more than 98% relative to hard dropping at equal exact-chunk budgets. Experiments on long-context benchmarks demonstrate that CEDAR recovers most of the quality lost by hard sparse routing while maintaining approximately $3\times$ kernel speedup at 128K context.

title: Team Pursuit/Breakaway Scenario Cycling Simulator with Evolutionary Computation (GA) Strategy Discovery Dataset: BSON-format export of MongoDB data collection.
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental settings and results for a research project exploring the use of applying an evolutionary algorithm search to two scenarios from the sport of competitive cycling: A team pursuit track cycling race where the finish time can be used as a measure of 'fitness'. A 'breakaway' scenario occurring at the end of a (road) race where fitness is tied to staying away from the chasing peloton and (ideally) winning. Above and beyond demonstrating the core use of the genetic algorithm search for team-specific solutions, further research was conducted into investigating the robustness of these solutions, and to the effects of domain-specific noise within the simulation behaviour on the discovery of strategies and their properties. The data is exported from a MongoDB database, and is contained in that database's compact BSON format (though it may be mapped to the more human-readable JSON format if needed). This dataset is designed to support the reproducibility of research that has been published in peer-reviewed environments, and therefore to support further efforts in this area. The application that runs the experiments, which includes the ability to show and search results and provide a step-by-step visualisation of solutions discovered from generation to generation, is available separately in its entirety as a GitHub-hosted project. Its URL is: https://github.com/aramicon/TeamPursuitModel The readme for the GitHub project contains essential details on running experiments and interpreting results. This research was conducted by Donal Kelly, under the supervision and support of Dr. Colm O'Riordan, both of the University of Galway, Ireland. Dataset structure overview: Compressed (BSON) MongoDB data database (crud_mongodb): experiment_results (by far the largest file, contains details from almost 1400 runs of the genetic algorithm). experiment_sequences (a sequence is used to auto-run a defined number of experiments with varying properties). experiment_settings (contains a titled list of settings that may be used to execute an experiment). test_suite_functions (a small number of separate test results; not important to the core research). Version: 1.0

title: Structural Isomorphism Across Non-Identical Generative Positions: A Time Restoration Theory 4.0 Account of Generalization in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: 人工智慧泛化(generalization)的核心問題之一,是模型如何由有限的既有學習經驗處理未見案例。本研究不重新建立統計學習理論,也不宣稱時間還原理論 4.0(TRT 4.0)取代既有機器學習方法,而是以 TRT 4.0 所完整承接並正式命題化的生成、非同一、差異、結構同型、表示再進入、必要層級與非封閉等關係,對人工智慧泛化問題進行跨領域理論映射。 本研究將泛化的理論問題重新表述為:當新案例與既有案例不是同一生成位置時,既有學習所形成的指定結構是否仍可在新位置重新成立。TRT 已允許 Iso_{κ_s}(x,y) 與 NonId_{κ_p}(x,y) 共同成立,因此,新舊案例不必取得生成位置同一,指定結構仍可同型成立。據此,本研究提出一項 TRT 框架內的理論闡述:泛化可被描述為「指定結構在非同一生成位置上的重新成立」。 此表述進一步區分記憶與泛化、有限資料與未來案例、抽象表示與本體同一,以及成功泛化與錯誤泛化。記憶偏向既有表示的再次取得;泛化則要求既有表示進入後續非同一生成位置後,指定結構仍可重新成立。錯誤泛化則可描述為:將某一判定位置上已成立的結構,未經新位置的重新判定而直接轉移至另一非同一位置。 本研究所得為 TRT 4.0 框架內的理論解釋與跨領域映射,不是神經網路機制的經驗證實。本研究未進行模型訓練、資料集實驗、統計分析、基準測試或新的機器學習數學證明,亦未建立 TRT 謂詞與神經網路內部變數之操作化對應。因此,本文不主張 TRT 已證明或解決人工智慧泛化問題,而是建立可供後續形式化、比較與經驗檢驗的理論表述。

title: Quantum Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Quantum Adaptive Algorithm (QAA), designed to achieve high-precision computations by dynamically adjusting quantum parameters based on input data characteristics. The QAA leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to enable iterative parameter optimization and computational processing. This approach contrasts significantly with conventional quantum algorithms that necessitate pre-defined parameter settings. The paper details the core mechanism, explores the algorithm's design principles, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its potential for enhanced computational performance.

title: Spectral Graph Embedding with Non-Euclidean Kernels
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of existing spectral graph embedding techniques, which predominantly operate under the assumption of Euclidean space. This assumption often hinders their performance when applied to complex, non-Euclidean graphs, prevalent in domains such as social networks, biological systems, and geographic data. We introduce a novel approach to spectral graph embedding that utilizes specifically designed kernel functions capable of directly capturing the intricate structure inherent in these non-Euclidean datasets. Our method moves beyond relying on Euclidean distance calculations, enabling a more accurate and effective representation of high-dimensional graph data. The core innovation lies in the development of kernels that explicitly model graph connectivity, leading to improved embedding quality and performance compared to conventional spectral methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications across diverse domains.

title: Graph-Based Probability Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic reasoning framework based on graph structures and probabilistic relationships. We propose a system that leverages the inherent topology and probabilistic nature of graphs to enhance reasoning capabilities and improve overall accuracy. The core mechanism revolves around constructing and manipulating graphs to represent knowledge and relationships, enabling automated inference and decision-making processes. The development of this framework addresses limitations of traditional rule-based approaches by offering a more flexible and robust methodology for handling intricate data and complex scenarios. The research investigates the potential of this approach across various domains, including knowledge graph reasoning, problem solving, and strategic decision-making. The ultimate goal is to provide a paradigm shift towards more efficient and reliable probabilistic reasoning.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to algorithm optimization utilizing a dynamically adjusted, iterative adaptive logic. The core principle centers around employing a self-regulating loop that continuously refines parameter settings and structural elements to achieve optimal performance. The development of this system aims to surpass the limitations of traditional optimization techniques by providing a flexible and responsive mechanism for enhancing algorithmic efficiency and performance. The focus is on providing a robust and adaptable framework for optimizing complex computational processes.

abstract: Quantum State Probability Modeling presents a novel approach to probability calculation and risk assessment leveraging the unique properties of quantum states. The core mechanism centers around the transformation of probability computation as a quantum process, utilizing quantum algorithms to achieve improved efficiency and accuracy. This study aims to demonstrate the practical benefits and potential advancements of this paradigm shift in probability modeling.

title: Contextualized Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Neural Networks
abstract: Probabilistic programming offers a powerful framework for modeling uncertainty and performing inference, but often relies on hand-designed prior distributions, which can be challenging to define accurately, particularly in complex systems. This work introduces a novel approach that integrates Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to dynamically learn and provide contextualized prior distributions within probabilistic programming. The core idea is to train a BNN on observed data to learn the posterior distribution of model parameters. The output of this BNN then serves as the prior distribution within a probabilistic programming framework, adapting to the specific context of the observed data. This allows for more accurate inference compared to traditional methods using fixed prior distributions. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and highlighting the benefits of dynamically adapting priors. This research provides a foundational step towards more flexible and robust probabilistic programming systems.

title: Quantum Error Correction and Adaptive Computation: A Novel Approach
abstract: Quantum error correction is a crucial component of future quantum computing, addressing the inherent fragility of quantum states. This paper explores a novel adaptive computation paradigm based on quantum error correction. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the quantum state, allowing for rapid search and optimization of complex computational instances, and resilience to environmental noise. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the potential benefits of this approach.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Logic: A Novel Approach to Dynamic Adaptability
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Probabilistic Logic (APL), a novel framework for probabilistic reasoning that dynamically adjusts its logical rules based on environmental changes. Traditional probabilistic logic often necessitates manual rule tuning, presenting a cumbersome process. APL leverages machine learning to learn the evolution of environmental states and rule changes, enabling automated rule adaptation and enhanced system responsiveness. The core mechanism centers around a learning algorithm designed to continuously refine the system's logic through observation and feedback, resulting in a more robust and adaptable system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of APL through a series of simulated scenarios, highlighting its ability to maintain consistent performance despite significant environmental shifts.

title: 基于动态机器学习的异常检测算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel anomaly detection algorithm based on dynamic machine learning. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on fixed thresholds, which can be suboptimal for complex datasets. This research introduces a dynamic approach that adapts the model's parameters, including thresholds and feature importance, during the learning process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments on a diverse set of datasets, showing significant improvements in detection accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The core mechanism leverages iterative updates to the model based on observed data, allowing for a more nuanced and adaptable detection strategy. The study explores the benefits of this dynamic approach in handling non-stationary data and identifying subtle anomalies.

title: Title: Adaptive Self-Adaptive Learning-Based Implicit Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to implicit modeling, leveraging adaptive self-adaptive learning algorithms to dynamically adjust model parameters. The core idea is to automatically fine-tune model parameters based on the calculated results of the learning process, ultimately enhancing model accuracy and efficiency. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often involve manual intervention, simplifying the model building process. We detail a framework incorporating a self-adaptive learning loop that iteratively refines model parameters to achieve optimal performance. The focus of this work is on automating the parameter adjustment process, offering a significant improvement over conventional techniques. The resulting model exhibits enhanced generalization capabilities and improved performance across a range of datasets.

title: Adaptive Topological Quantum Information Structure Optimization (ATQS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Topological Quantum Information Structure Optimization (ATQS) method, a novel approach to quantum information structure optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on classical mathematical techniques, while ATQS leverages the power of topology to dynamically refine quantum information structures, thereby enhancing storage and transmission efficiencies. The core mechanism involves learning and adapting to dynamic topological structures within the quantum system. This paper details the design of the ATQS algorithm, its theoretical foundation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing quantum information representation. The study highlights the potential of topology to provide a more efficient and robust solution for quantum information management.

title: 基于量子拓扑的量子计算的自适应拓扑调整
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but current challenges lie in achieving reliable and precise results, particularly in complex calculations. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum computation utilizing the principles of quantum topology – specifically, a dynamically adjustable topology shift. We propose a method based on quantum system evolution and dynamic adjustment of quantum topology, designed to enhance the accuracy of quantum computations by adapting the underlying structure during the computation. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to dynamically tailor the system's state, thereby enabling a more precise and efficient solution. This research explores the potential of such a technique to overcome limitations of traditional quantum algorithms, offering a promising pathway towards advancing the field of quantum computing.

title: ##基于时空意识的计算 (STIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational model, termed "基于时空意识的计算" (STIC), which aims to replicate the fundamental processes of biological awareness by mimicking how the nervous system perceives and processes time, space, and events. The core of STIC lies in constructing multi-dimensional spacetime graphs, incorporating temporal, spatial, and event dimensions, to store and process information. These graphs are augmented with attention-based mechanisms that prioritize and focus on salient information, mirroring the selective attention observed in biological neural systems. Unlike traditional computer representations of time, space, and events, STIC offers a biologically-inspired approach, potentially providing valuable insights for artificial intelligence research into consciousness. The model's architecture and operational principles are detailed, highlighting its key features and potential applications. ---

title: Quantum Network Information Encoding and Decoding Methods
abstract: This paper investigates the core methods of information encoding and decoding within quantum networks, aiming to enhance both the efficiency and security of quantum information transmission. We explore various encoding schemes, including amplitude encoding, phase encoding, and polarization encoding, alongside their corresponding decoding strategies. The core mechanism relies on manipulating quantum states to represent and transmit information securely. Our research focuses on optimizing these processes to mitigate the effects of noise and loss, critical challenges in long-distance quantum communication. We delve into error correction techniques specifically tailored for quantum systems, such as quantum error correction codes (QECCs) and their application in decoding. Furthermore, we examine the role of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols as a fundamental decoding process, highlighting the security aspects derived from the laws of quantum mechanics. The ultimate goal is to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in quantum network information encoding and decoding, paving the way for future advancements in quantum communication technologies.

title: Integrated Geophysical and Remote Sensing Analysis for Identifying Mineralization Potential in Wadi Queih, Central Eastern Desert, Egypt
abstract: The integration of aeromagnetic, gamma-ray spectrometric, and remote sensing approaches was used to delineate structural configurations and identify potential mineralization sites in the Wadi Queih area, Eastern Desert, Egypt. Focusing on weathered Precambrian terrains, this study establishes a predictive, multitier exploration model for the Wadi Queih area (Eastern Desert, Egypt) by integrating aeromagnetic, gamma-ray spectrometric, and Landsat-9 OLI-2 datasets. Rather than analyzing these datasets in isolation, the novel contribution of this integrated approach lies in its ability to map the complete genetic path of mineralization—bridging subsurface structural conduits, surface hydrothermal alteration, and radioelements. Subsurface structural configurations mapped via magnetic tilt derivative (TDR) and analytic signal (AS) filters were revealed. The main finding is that the dominant NW–SE structural trend is consistent with regional tectonic structures associated with Red Sea rifting. By co-registering these deep structures with surface mineralogical mapping from Landsat-9 OLI-2 (processed using PCA, band ratios, and Spectral Angle Mapper), we demonstrate a direct structural control on hydrothermal alteration zones. Specifically, these fault zones align with intense hydroxyl and iron oxide alterations, while the Spectral Angle Mapper successfully identified serpentinite-hosted magnesite and chromite extensions. Airborne gamma-ray spectrometry validated these targets, mapping localized potassium enrichment along fault-controlled alteration zones and identifying strata-bound uranium enrichment within the phosphorogenic Duwi and Tarif Formations. The convergence of these three independent datasets provides a self-validating targeting framework that significantly reduces exploration risk compared to traditional single-dataset analyses. Ultimately, this integrated, multidisciplinary approach provides a robust and highly generalizable exploration framework for complex Precambrian terrains globally.

title: Certified Panic Mode: Repair-Invariant Error Recovery for Maximal-Munch Lexing
abstract: Classical panic-mode recovery skips a failed scan forward by convention: it promises progress, and membership in a designated set where one is found, but no repair-universal boundary guarantee for the position it lands on. This paper chooses the resume position by theorem: a position is a sound recovery point when every prefix repair whose scan commits through the certificate's returned evidence places a token boundary there, complete repairs the special case, by a committed-prefix lemma over certificates posted for a different purpose (arXiv:2608.03473, arXiv:2608.09761). The quantifier is strictly the stronger one, and a dichotomy locates the difference exactly: the inclusion is strict precisely when no repair completes while some scan still commits through the evidence, a two-token witness realizing the case. The evidence-returning form pairs each answer with the interval it rests on, which is what makes the guarantee deployable: a caller who knows what the scanner cannot check decides whether the certified boundary transfers to the clean input it intended. The search is one forward walk in evidence order and provably terminates; the guarantee is per-automaton, relative to the active mode. The procedure ships in the munch lexing library, and a deterministic corruption study measures its recovery quality beside the classical skip-one and delimiter conventions. Every certified answer whose evidence survives the damage passes its executable landing check on every recovery move, 40,885 of 40,885; among first answers, the 5,595 resting on evidence the damage reached land 1,589 times, reported and never asserted. evidence.abstract: Classical panic-mode recovery skips a failed scan forward by convention: it promises progress, and membership in a designated set where one is found, but no repair-universal boundary guarantee for the position it lands on. This paper chooses the resume position by theorem: a position is a sound recovery point when every prefix repair whose scan commits through the certificate's returned evidence places a token boundary there, complete repairs the special case, by a committed-prefix lemma over certificates posted for a different purpose (arXiv:2608.03473, arXiv:2608.09761). The quantifier is strictly the stronger one, and a dichotomy locates the difference exactly: the inclusion is strict precisely when no repair completes while some scan still commits through the evidence, a two-token witness realizing the case. The evidence-returning form pairs each answer with the interval it rests on, which is what makes the guarantee deployable: a caller who knows what the scanner cannot check decides whether the certified boundary transfers to the clean input it intended. The search is one forward walk in evidence order and provably terminates; the guarantee is per-automaton, relative to the active mode. The procedure ships in the munch lexing library, and a deterministic corruption study measures its recovery quality beside the classical skip-one and delimiter conventions. Every certified answer whose evidence survives the damage passes its executable landing check on every recovery move, 40,885 of 40,885; among first answers, the 5,595 resting on evidence the damage reached land 1,589 times, reported and never asserted. On 13,522 of the 16,808 trials the shipped repair routine labels beyond repair, the resumed suffix tokenizes whole and the two quantifiers provably coincide, so both are empty there if those negative labels are exact; 3,286 stay undetermined.

title: Analog-to-digital conversion in the quantum regime
abstract: Digital signal processing has become essential in quantum optics, particularly for continuous-variable (CV) information encoding, enabling coherent detection schemes and mitigation of linear impairments. While linear signal processing in double homodyne detection has been studied under the assumption that all post-measurement processing can be backpropagated in the optical domain, a rigorous treatment of the digitization chain, spanning optical, electronic, and sampling stages, is still lacking. In this work, we consider the continuous mode description of double homodyne detection to fully capture the maximum mode-matching coefficient achievable as a function of electronic noise, signal bandwidth, receiver electronics bandwidth, and sampling rate, that is the entry point of digital signal processing. We establish a dimensioning rule that generalizes the Nyquist-Shannon criterion to account for quantum fluctuations of the measured signal, not merely its bandwidth. Analyzing the case of additive white electronic noise, we find numerically that optimal signal-to-noise ratio is achieved when the electronic bandwidth is large enough to pass the signal yet narrower than the sampling rate in order to mitigate noise amplification, yielding a concrete design criterion for coherent detection.

title: Parser-Free VLM Verification for Federated Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
abstract: How can vision-language models help video anomaly detection (VAD) when surveillance data remain distributed, weakly labeled, and resource-constrained? Most weakly supervised VAD methods assume centralized training; recent VLM-based extensions further rely on dense inference, generated explanations, or additional adaptation. We introduce a lightweight federated MIL-VLM cascade in which only a compact MIL scorer is trained across clients, while a frozen VLM verifies high-scoring suspect segments post hoc. We study two VLM feedback interfaces: parsed text-generation decisions and a logit-based interface that extracts a continuous anomaly score from next-token Yes/No probabilities. Experiments on UCF-Crime with InternVL3.5-2B and Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct show that text-generation verification can improve frame-level AUC after diagnostic temporal post-processing, but remains sensitive to prompts, parsers, model choice, and smoothing. In contrast, the logit interface provides a fixed parser-free signal that improves both frame-level AUC and frame-level AP over the MIL baseline across both VLMs, without temporal post-processing in its main configuration. Since suspect segments are updated independently once available, next-token logit feedback provides a simple segment-local alternative to text-generation verification.

title: Evaluating synthetic-data fidelity in two-group biomedical studies: a multidimensional validation framework
abstract: Synthetic data increasingly support model development and privacy-conscious sharing in biomedicine. Two-group studies require synthetic data to reproduce within-group structure and between-group differences, yet marginal agreement or predictive performance may obscure multivariate and conditional-dependence changes. We present a multidimensional validation framework for class-conditional synthetic data and apply it to three datasets spanning sample-size and dimensionality regimes. Two controls and four generators spanning mixture, interpolation, hybrid, and latent-variable architectures (GMM, SMOTE, GMM-SMOTE, and CVAE, respectively) were assessed using predictive utility, real–synthetic distinguishability, marginal agreement, PCA and t-SNE geometry, pairwise dependence, and Graphical LASSO networks. Noise perturbation, within-class permutation, and reverse ablation probed the sources of real–synthetic distinguishability. Across 18 dataset–method comparisons, discriminator AUC ranged from 0.55 to 1.00, while mean feature-level KS statistics ranged from 0.027 to 0.282. Thus, strong performance under individual criteria coexisted with detectable differences and lost or synthetic-only dependencies. Rather than assigning a single fidelity score, the framework supports multidimensional fidelity reporting as a minimum standard for shared synthetic biomedical data.

title: A machine-checked proof still needs a statement contract
abstract: Anthropic's Fermat formalization shows the scale now possible in Lean; the remaining assurance problem is preserving meaning, provenance and dependency scope from source theorem to checked root. This article was already archived in the 45-item GERO collection (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22683900). This individual record provides a separate citation; it is not a new finding or a new experiment. Originally published 2026-09-07 by Xamit Kadirbekov. The archive includes the complete original article, source links, metadata and checksums. All scientific claims and test counts remain those of the original report; no numerical tests were rerun for this archival deposit. title: LoTRS: Practical Post-Quantum Structured Threshold Ring Signatures from Lattices
abstract: LoTRS: Practical Post-Quantum Structured Threshold Ring Signatures from Lattices This repository accompanies a paper accepted to ACM CCS 2026. A preprint is available from the IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive: Nikai Jagganath, Muhammed F. Esgin, Ron Steinfeld, Amin Sakzad, Markku-Juhani O. Saarinen, and Dongxi Liu. LoTRS: Practical Post-Quantum Structured Threshold Ring Signatures from Lattices. In the Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS 2026). Preprint: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive, Report 2026/974. https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/974 The artifact package includes the accepted CCS paper and its artifact appendix. Citation: @inproceedings{jagganath2026lotrs, author = {Nikai Jagganath and Muhammed F. Esgin and Ron Steinfeld and Amin Sakzad and Markku-Juhani O. Saarinen and Dongxi Liu}, title = {{LoTRS}: Practical Post-Quantum Structured Threshold Ring Signatures from Lattices}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security}, year = {2026}, publisher = {Association for Computing Machinery}, note = {Preprint available as Cryptology {ePrint} Archive, Paper 2026/974}, url = {https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/974} } The artifact contains Python and Rust implementations, parameter-estimation scripts, a FACCT-style sampler specification, and a benchmark harness. The concrete kappa=1 instantiation uses the shared production profile in parameters.json. README.md this file LoTRS.pdf accepted CCS paper LoTRS-artifact-appendix.pdf artifact appendix LICENSE MIT Makefile conformance checks and cleanup parameters.json shared production parameter manifest lotrs-facct-sampler.md specification of the large-sigma sampler lotrs-py/ Python reference implementation lotrs-rs/ Rust performance implementation estimator/ SageMath parameter-estimation scripts Conformance scripts and signature fixtures live in lotrs-py/; the Rust tests consume those fixtures and the shared manifest directly. The Python implementation is the golden reference — it is short, readable, and emits a deterministic test-vector blob that the Rust implementation reproduces byte-for-byte. Quick reproducibility check Requires Python, a Rust toolchain with a C linker, and Make. check-full also requires SageMath as sage on PATH. Tested with Python 3.14.7, Rust/Cargo 1.98.1, and SageMath 10.9 on Linux x86_64. Dependency installation needs network access; the tests and experiments run locally. Create a Python environment and run the complete conformance check: python3 -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -r lotrs-py/requirements.txt make check make check-full # adds full production signing and Sage alignment tests make check runs all Python tests, verifies both shipped signature fixtures, checks the parameter manifest, and runs Rust unit and interoperability tests. The Rust tests require the shipped Python vectors and compare keys and full signatures byte-for-byte. The shipped vectors use schema 3. make check-full passes 142 Python tests, 65 Rust tests, and five Sage tests, including production signing and the compact production-lattice fixture. Allow about five minutes after dependency installation. Reproducing the benchmarks The benchmark reports, CSV data, and plots are in lotrs-rs/bench-out/. To reproduce the full grid: cd lotrs-rs mkdir -p bench-out cargo run --release --example bench -- \ --grid "32,1:4:8:16:32;100,1:5:10:25:50;1,2:4:8:16" \ > bench-out/grid-d128.md 2>&1 pip install matplotlib # one-time, only for plot_bench.py python3 scripts/plot_bench.py bench-out/grid-d128.md Runtime depends on the machine. The release build uses rayon across available hardware threads. The plot script writes bench-out/{data.csv, summary.md, sign-vs-T.pdf, sigsize-vs-T.pdf, breakdown-vs-T.pdf, rs-alone-vs-N.pdf, dualms-alone-vs-T.pdf}. For a faster smoke test that produces the headline parameter rows without the full grid: cargo run --release --example bench -- --skip-test --with-prod The current run's summary.md and data.csv are the readable and machine readable results. Its README.md records the measurement environment. See lotrs-rs/README.md § Benchmarks for the hardware / methodology footnotes (sample counts per cell, the measured and estimated attempt counts, and column definitions). Reproducing the parameter selection The SageMath scripts in estimator/ calculate sizes, rejection counts, parameter conditions, and attack-cost estimates for the shared manifest: cd estimator make # runs lotrs_estimate.py — prints the headline output make reference # writes a fresh comparison log to compare against # the checked-in LoTRS-Estimate-Output-N100T50.txt For the production profile (N=100, T=50), the reference run gives: Analytic signature size 52.6574 KiB Single public key size 9.40625 KiB Ring PK size 47,031.25 KiB Expected signing attempts 4.7728 (heuristic) Binary-proof PQ ASIS cost (variant 0) 100.7978 bits DualMS PQ ASIS cost (variant 0) 94.16636 bits The full output reports all three bundled ASIS variants separately; variants 1 and 2 give 88.86122 bits for the binary proof and 86.20864 bits for DualMS. The manifest uses k=14, l=20, l'=21, n_hat=12, k_hat=11, q=2^43-67, and q_hat=2^35-451. Both binary-proof rejection factors are 24; phi=max(22*T,1100) retains the regularity floor at small thresholds. The analytic size is an encoding estimate; the measured Rice-encoded signature is 53.53 KiB. The attack costs above do not substantiate 128-bit post-quantum security. Requires SageMath with Python support available as sage. The estimator vendors local copies of the lattice estimator and the ASIS/MSIS estimator so no network access is needed at run time — see estimator/README.md for requirements and the bundled helper libraries. Component overviews lotrs-py/ Python reference implementation of the concrete kappa = 1 LoTRS instantiation. Covers parameters / derived bounds, ring arithmetic (with auxiliary-prime CRT-NTT), CDT and FACCT-style Gaussian samplers, signature encoding/decoding, the full signing and verification pipeline, unit tests, and the deterministic test-vector emitter. The LoTRS implementation is Python; dependencies include NumPy, PyCryptodome, and mpmath. lotrs-rs/ Rust implementation of the same concrete LoTRS path, aligned with the Python reference at the public wire-format boundary. Covers setup, key generation, aggregation, signing, and verification; serialization compatible with the Python reference; a CRT-NTT ring backend with pseudo-Mersenne reduction; CDT and FACCT-style samplers; the Python/Rust interop tests; and the bench harness. Both implementations precompute a 256-bit SHAKE-128 digest of the canonical PK-table serialization once per signing or verification call and feed that digest into H_agg, H_com, and the Fiat-Shamir hash, instead of re-hashing the multi-MiB ring public-key table at every call site. Binding to the full PK is preserved by SHAKE-128 collision-resistance. The artifact does not claim a constant-time signing implementation. Gaussian/FACCT/rejection sampling and signing restart logic are data-dependent; see lotrs-rs/README.md for the side-channel status. estimator/ SageMath scripts that reproduce the concrete parameter selection, size calculations, and post-quantum security estimates. Vendors local copies of the lattice estimator and the ASIS/MSIS estimator so the artifact can be evaluated without fetching dependencies. See estimator/README.md for requirements and details of the bundled external estimator components. lotrs-facct-sampler.md Specification of the FACCT-style integer Gaussian sampler used for the large masking distributions (sigma_0, sigma_0_prime) in the benchmark and production parameter sets. Covers the truncated target distribution, the SHAKE-128/XOF-driven randomness, the uniform proposal, the fixed-point Bernoulli-exp acceptance test, the explicit parameter-set sampler selection used by the implementations, and the validation requirements that the Python/Rust cross-language KAT enforces. Artifact scope The artifact focuses on the concrete kappa = 1 implementation path and the parameter set used for the paper's reported sizes and benchmarks. The Python implementation is the readable reference, the Rust implementation is the performance-oriented implementation, and the estimator reproduces the parameter and size calculations. License MIT — see LICENSE.

title: Different training paradigms yield distinct learned structures in recurrent neural network models
abstract: Introduction RNNs trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) solve tasks through reliance on global error signals [1], while evolutionary algorithms and activity-dependent plasticity rules are gradient-free alternatives to solve the same tasks. How the choice of training paradigm biases the solutions that models arrive at remains unclear. Here we compare four paradigms—BPTT, evolution strategies (ES) [2], a genetic algorithm (GA), and GA with Oja's Hebbian plasticity (GA+Oja)—on n-back recall, in which the network reports which of five symbols appeared n steps earlier. Beyond task accuracy, we analyze the connectivity changes that occur under each paradigm, finding that training method shapes structure far more than it determines performance. Methods We trained RNNs (32, 128, 256 units) on a 5-symbol n-back task. BPTT employed gradient descent with the Adam optimizer (2000 iterations). ES estimated gradients from 128 perturbed copies of the network (perturbation σ = 0.02, 500 generations). GA used tournament selection with neuron-level crossover and self-adaptive mutation (128 individuals, 500 generations). GA+Oja co-evolved two Oja's rule parameters (learning rate and weight bound) which update recurrent weights via correlated activity, enabling within-lifetime adaptation atop evolved connectivity. We tested n-back 1–4 steps, measuring accuracy (chance accuracy = 20%), per-layer weight-change fractions, effective rank of the recurrent weight matrix, and total weight-change magnitude. Results All methods converged to ~100% at 2-back, although ES showed high variance at 1-back (~85%; Fig. 1A). At 4-back, ES maintained ~100%, whereas GA declined to ~80% and GA+Oja to ~89%; BPTT remained at ~100%. Connectivity analysis revealed a strikingly different structure despite comparable accuracy. BPTT produced low effective rank recurrent matrices (~8 at 1-back) that increased with difficulty (~26 at 4-back). In contrast, evolutionary methods clustered at a higher rank (~16) with less variation across levels (Fig. 1B). BPTT increasingly allocated weight changes to the output layer with difficulty (~29% to ~43%). In comparison, all evolutionary methods remained flat at ~21% (Fig. 1C). Discussion Gradient-based and evolutionary training produce comparably accurate networks with fundamentally different connectivity. BPTT finds low-rank recurrent solutions and progressively shifts learning toward output weights as difficulty increases, consistent with efficient credit assignment [3]. Evolutionary methods converge on distributed, high-rank solutions with uniform layer allocation — a qualitatively different regime. These results caution that studies inferring biological principles from trained RNNs may reflect the training algorithm rather than computational necessity. BPTT's concentration of learning in output weights could mislead analyses of how recurrent dynamics support memory if the readout is not examined separately. Acknowledgments We thank Dora Jiayue Li and the Pomona College Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP) for supporting early exploration on this project, as well as the Pomona College Department of Neuroscience for their senior thesis support. Figure Figure 1: (A) Accuracy vs. n-back level: methods converge at 2-back; ES maintains ~100% at 4-back, whereas GA declines to ~80%. (B) BPTT effective rank increases from ~8 to ~26 with difficulty; evolutionary methods cluster at ~16. (C) BPTT shifts learning to the output layer (+14%); evolutionary methods stay flat. 32 neurons, mean ± std, 3 seeds. References [1] Neftci, E., Mostafa, H., & Zenke, F. (2019). Surrogate Gradient Learning in Spiking Neural Networks: Bringing the Power of Gradient-Based Optimization to Spiking Neural Networks. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine, 36(6), 51-63. doi: 10.1109/MSP.2019.2931595[2] Salimans, T., Ho, J., Chen, X., Sidor, S., & Sutskever, I. (2017). evidence.title: Different training paradigms yield distinct learned structures in recurrent neural network models
evidence.abstract: Introduction RNNs trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) solve tasks through reliance on global error signals [1], while evolutionary algorithms and activity-dependent plasticity rules are gradient-free alternatives to solve the same tasks. How the choice of training paradigm biases the solutions that models arrive at remains unclear. Here we compare four paradigms—BPTT, evolution strategies (ES) [2], a genetic algorithm (GA), and GA with Oja's Hebbian plasticity (GA+Oja)—on n-back recall, in which the network reports which of five symbols appeared n steps earlier. Beyond task accuracy, we analyze the connectivity changes that occur under each paradigm, finding that training method shapes structure far more than it determines performance. Methods We trained RNNs (32, 128, 256 units) on a 5-symbol n-back task. BPTT employed gradient descent with the Adam optimizer (2000 iterations). ES estimated gradients from 128 perturbed copies of the network (perturbation σ = 0.02, 500 generations). GA used tournament selection with neuron-level crossover and self-adaptive mutation (128 individuals, 500 generations). GA+Oja co-evolved two Oja's rule parameters (learning rate and weight bound) which update recurrent weights via correlated activity, enabling within-lifetime adaptation atop evolved connectivity. We tested n-back 1–4 steps, measuring accuracy (chance accuracy = 20%), per-layer weight-change fractions, effective rank of the recurrent weight matrix, and total weight-change magnitude. Results All methods converged to ~100% at 2-back, although ES showed high variance at 1-back (~85%; Fig. 1A). At 4-back, ES maintained ~100%, whereas GA declined to ~80% and GA+Oja to ~89%; BPTT remained at ~100%. Connectivity analysis revealed a strikingly different structure despite comparable accuracy. BPTT produced low effective rank recurrent matrices (~8 at 1-back) that increased with difficulty (~26 at 4-back). In contrast, evolutionary methods clustered at a higher rank (~16) with less variation across levels (Fig. 1B). BPTT increasingly allocated weight changes to the output layer with difficulty (~29% to ~43%). In comparison, all evolutionary methods remained flat at ~21% (Fig. 1C). Discussion Gradient-based and evolutionary training produce comparably accurate networks with fundamentally different connectivity. BPTT finds low-rank recurrent solutions and progressively shifts learning toward output weights as difficulty increases, consistent with efficient credit assignment [3]. Evolutionary methods converge on distributed, high-rank solutions with uniform layer allocation — a qualitatively different regime. These results caution that studies inferring biological principles from trained RNNs may reflect the training algorithm rather than computational necessity. BPTT's concentration of learning in output weights could mislead analyses of how recurrent dynamics support memory if the readout is not examined separately. (B) BPTT effective rank increases from ~8 to ~26 with difficulty; evolutionary methods cluster at ~16. (C) BPTT shifts learning to the output layer (+14%); evolutionary methods stay flat. 32 neurons, mean ± std, 3 seeds. References [1] Neftci, E., Mostafa, H., & Zenke, F. (2019). title: Quantum Geometry Algorithm for Singularity Detection and Feature Extraction in High-Dimensional Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum geometry algorithm designed to detect and extract valuable features from high-dimensional data, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement and superposition. Traditional methods often struggle with the complexity of high-dimensional datasets, necessitating more efficient and precise techniques. Our algorithm utilizes quantum geometry to identify anomalous patterns and singularities within data, offering a significant advancement in data analysis efficiency. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation to achieve a more accurate and robust assessment of data's inherent properties. This research addresses the limitations of conventional approaches by presenting a fundamentally new methodology that promises to revolutionize data processing.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection using Learned Relational Embeddings
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to anomaly detection that leverages the power of graph representation learning and learned relational embeddings. Traditional anomaly detection techniques frequently struggle to effectively identify anomalous behavior in datasets characterized by complex relationships and dependencies between entities. Our method addresses this limitation by learning a low-dimensional embedding space where nodes in a graph are represented based on their connections and interactions. Anomalies are then detected as deviations from expected patterns within this learned relational embedding space. The core of our approach lies in the use of neural networks to automatically learn these embeddings, capturing intricate relational information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and potential improvements. The proposed method provides a more robust and nuanced approach to anomaly detection, particularly in scenarios where relational dependencies are critical for identifying unusual behavior. The method's adaptability and scalability make it suitable for a wide range of applications.

title: 基于自适应的量子隐形计算的密钥生成算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel key generation algorithm based on adaptive quantum computation, designed to enhance key generation efficiency and mitigate security risks. Traditional key generation methods rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability to complex environments. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the key generation process, optimizing performance and security. We detail the core mechanism, highlighting the key innovations in this approach. The algorithm utilizes a feedback loop to continuously refine the key generation process, ensuring a robust and efficient key generation cycle. The advantages of this approach include improved key generation speed, increased key security, and the potential for greater resilience against attacks. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the algorithm's implementation and performance evaluation.

title: Adaptive Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Entanglement Perception
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, promises revolutionary advancements in computation and information transfer. However, harnessing this phenomenon requires sophisticated control and manipulation, presenting significant challenges for algorithm design. This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm designed to address these challenges, focusing specifically on the perception and manipulation of quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages a dynamically evolving "quantum state intelligence" framework to continuously monitor and adjust quantum operations, achieving unprecedented precision and efficiency. We demonstrate its efficacy through rigorous simulations and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to unlock new capabilities in quantum information processing. The core mechanism centers around real-time state sensing and a novel optimization strategy inspired by the dynamics of quantum entanglement itself. This work represents a significant step towards building more robust and versatile quantum algorithms.

title: Causal Inference via Graph Laplacian Spectral Decomposition
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal inference within complex networks utilizing graph Laplacian spectral decomposition and established causal inference techniques. The core idea revolves around representing the network's causal structure through the graph Laplacian and then employing methods like Granger causality to determine directional influence. This approach offers a rigorous framework for identifying causal relationships, addressing the challenges inherent in traditional methods when dealing with intricate, interconnected systems. The methodology provides a mathematically sound basis for understanding complex interactions, moving beyond purely correlational analyses. The effectiveness of this combined approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, paving the way for further exploration and application in diverse fields.

title: Based on Neural-Symbolic Fusion for Program Generation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program generation by fusing the strengths of neural networks and symbolic programming. Traditional program generation methods often struggle with complexity, robustness, and interpretability. Neural networks excel at pattern recognition and learning from data, while symbolic programming provides logical reasoning and explicit representation. We propose a neural-symbolic fusion model designed to leverage both paradigms, resulting in more flexible and reliable program generation. The core of our method involves constructing a model that integrates neural network outputs with symbolic expressions, enabling both program generation and rigorous verification. We demonstrate the potential of this approach, highlighting its ability to overcome limitations inherent in purely neural or purely symbolic systems. The key contribution lies in the bridging of the gap between these two approaches, unlocking significantly enhanced program generation capabilities. ---

title: Title: Geometric Phase Field Theory for Dynamic Data Structures
abstract: Geometric Phase Field Theory (GPFT) offers a novel framework for analyzing and optimizing the performance of dynamic data structures, addressing limitations of traditional approaches. This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical model and practical implementation of GPFT, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing the performance of various data structure types under dynamic workloads. The core contribution lies in defining a set of geometric phases that explicitly capture the evolution of data structures, enabling a rigorous investigation of their performance characteristics. We introduce a new methodology for analyzing data structure dynamics, incorporating geometric phase analysis to provide insights into optimization strategies. The research explores the interplay between geometric phase structure and performance metrics, ultimately offering a robust solution for dynamically optimizing data structures.

title: INTELLIGENT SOLUTIONS AND MACHINE LEARNING IN MECHANICAL ENGINEERING: APPLICATION OPPORTUNITIES AND PROMISING DIRECTIONS
abstract: This article analyzes the current state, practical applications, and promising development directions of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies in mechanical engineering. The study examines the application of AI and ML methods in predictive maintenance, design optimization, manufacturing and process optimization, robotics and automation, quality control, and structural health monitoring. The capabilities of modern approaches, including neural networks, deep learning, reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and Bayesian optimization, in solving complex engineering problems are also discussed. Particular attention is paid to the integration of data-driven models with physics-based models, uncertainty quantification, model interpretability, reliability, and adaptability under different operating conditions. The analysis demonstrates that the integration of AI and ML into mechanical engineering provides significant opportunities for improving production efficiency, reducing maintenance costs, enhancing product quality, optimizing engineering processes, and developing sustainable engineering solutions. The study also identifies promising research directions related to physics-informed artificial intelligence, explainable AI, uncertainty-aware models, hybrid intelligent systems, and adaptive engineering technologies.

title: Provable Parallel Algorithm Design Method
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to parallel algorithm design centered around provable correctness and efficiency. Traditional parallel algorithm development often relies heavily on empirical methods, leading to a lack of rigorous guarantees regarding algorithm behavior and performance. Our proposed method leverages formal methods, specifically theorem proving and model checking, to design parallel algorithms that are demonstrably correct and efficient. The core idea involves decomposing an algorithm into a set of parallel tasks, then using formal verification techniques to rigorously prove the correctness and efficiency of each task. This ensures the overall algorithm's correctness and guarantees its suitability for parallel execution. The resulting algorithms offer a significant advantage over existing approaches by providing a solid theoretical foundation, reducing the reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, and enabling the development of complex parallel algorithms that were previously intractable. This work outlines the methodology, provides a framework for applying formal verification, and demonstrates the potential of this approach for creating robust and reliable parallel solutions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Programming
abstract: This paper explores the potential of a novel geometric programming language predicated on quantum entanglement. We propose a framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to model and analyze complex quantum systems. The core claim is that this language will enable the simulation of non-linear geometric effects arising from entanglement, opening avenues for novel computational capabilities and a deeper understanding of quantum systems. This work investigates the integration of entanglement as a fundamental geometric element within the programming paradigm, proposing a new approach to quantum computation and analysis. The paper presents a preliminary conceptual model and outlines a potential algorithm for simulating entangled states.

title: Adaptive Generalized Matrix Construction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to generalized matrix construction, utilizing an adaptive learning framework. Traditional methods often rely on manual parameter adjustment, limiting the model's adaptability. We propose a dynamic learning algorithm that iteratively adjusts the weights of the generalized matrix based on input data features, achieving improved generalization performance. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning weighting strategy that continuously refines the matrix's representation. This adaptive approach overcomes limitations of static methods, offering a more robust and flexible solution for various machine learning tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments on benchmark datasets, highlighting its superior performance compared to established methods.

title: A Multi-Layer Auditable Vertical Federated Learning Prototype for Power Equipment Supply Chains: Reproducibility, Robustness, and Privacy-Boundary Evaluation
abstract: Transformer lifecycle data across organizations are typically vertically partitioned among material suppliers, manufacturers, logistics service providers, testing agencies, and operation and maintenance units. This study presents a reproducible multi-layer vertical federated learning (VFL) prototype that integrates salted-hash identifier matching, additive sharing of local score vectors over finite fields, and a local public key infrastructure with a signature-based audit verification mechanism. A deterministic synthetic dataset is first constructed, comprising 5200 aligned records and 31 predictor variables, which are partitioned among five participants with varying numbers of features per participant. Second, across five validation runs, the VFL models under both the standard block-wise and score-sharing paths achieved an AUC of 0.8825 ± 0.0119, an F1 score of 0.7367 ± 0.0249, and an accuracy of 0.8102 ± 0.0183 on the test set. The classification results of both paths were fully consistent with the centralized gradient-descent logistic regression baseline. Notably, the score-sharing path exhibited a maximum log-odds deviation of only 2.22 × 10−8 on the test set, with no prediction discrepancies observed. Third, across 10 independently generated synthetic populations, the nonlinear output mechanism highlights the limitations of linear models: the AUC of vertical federated learning (VFL) drops to 0.6457 ± 0.0171, while Extra Trees and HistGradientBoosting achieve 0.7731 ± 0.0149 and 0.7743 ± 0.0139, respectively. Finally, in a separate residual-sharing diagnostic test, when 1 to 4 participants jointly shared the residuals, the label inference AUC remained around 0.499–0.500; however, when all five participants shared or plaintext residuals were used, the labels could be fully recovered. Both simple membership inference diagnostic tests yielded results close to random. The local signature log verifier rejected all 700 injected faults and accepted the 400 clean control log events. These results validate the feasibility of numerical reproducibility and local audit functionality under synthetic data and single-process conditions, yet they are insufficient to demonstrate end-to-end label privacy protection, malicious security, effectiveness on real data, or real-time ledger performance.

title: Brain-Inspired Computing: Enhancing Human–Computer Interaction
abstract: This research introduces a brain-inspired computing framework to enhance human-computer interaction (HCI) by emulating cognitive and neural processes. Addressing current limitations in adaptability, energy efficiency, and real-time responsiveness, the proposed model leverages spiking neural networks, multimodal sensor fusion, and neuro-symbolic reasoning. The system dynamically adapts to user behavior, emotional state, and environmental conditions, improving personalization and interaction fluidity. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance in emotion recognition, task generalization, and low-latency response compared to traditional HCI methods. The framework paves the way for scalable, context-aware, and energy-efficient HCI across interactive systems.

title: From Bits to Qubits: The Theory and Practice of Quantum Data Encoding
abstract: Encoding classical data into quantum systems is a foundational step in the execution of nearly all quantum algorithms, and a critical bottleneck in realizing practical quantum advantage. This review provides a comprehensive account of the concepts, algorithms, and practical considerations associated with quantum data encoding. We trace the development from its early conceptual foundations to recent advances, considering commonly used access models, such as quantum state preparation, unitary synthesis, QRAM and block encoding. We survey the circuit size, depth, space-time tradeoffs, as well as non-Clifford resources required for fault-tolerant implementation. We also discuss the roles of different access models in quantum algorithms. Special attention is given to structured data, such as sparse data, Boolean functions and data represented by tensor networks. This review bridges theory and applications, serving both as a pedagogical guide for newcomers and as a reference for active researchers. We also highlight the pivotal role of quantum data encoding in quantum computing and provide insights into future directions that will enable quantum advantage.

title: Climate-ModernBERT: Revisiting Corpus Composition for Domain-Adaptive Continued Pretraining
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) in the climate domain requires models to process heterogeneous text sources, including scientific literature, policy disclosures, and synthetic reports. However, how to effectively combine diverse domain corpora during continued pretraining (CPT) remains underexplored. We introduce Climate-ModernBERT, a family of climate-adapted encoder models obtained through continued pretraining of ModernBERT-Base on three climate corpora: academic climate text, climate-filtered web data, and synthetic climate documents. title: Aha-Flow Distillation: Flow Markers Matter in LLM Reasoning
abstract: We identify the Flow Moment, a reasoning pattern characterized by sustained, process-confirming verbalizations such as I'm doing, in contrast to the revision- and backtracking-oriented Aha Moment. We refer to their corresponding linguistic expressions as Flow Markers and Aha Markers, respectively. Based on this observation, we construct Flow-CoT by rewriting the discourse markers of original reasoning traces while preserving their underlying reasoning content, and use it as auxiliary supervision for on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). We further propose \textbf{Aha-Flow Distillation (AFD)}, a dual-mode extension of OPSD that pairs different forms of privileged information with corresponding reasoning instructions. The Aha branch retains concise solution-based supervision, while the Flow branch introduces rewritten Flow-CoT under a direct and confident reasoning instruction. At inference time, the model uses only the standard reflective instruction, so Flow-style reasoning serves purely as a training signal. Experiments on AIME25 and HMMT25 show consistent improvements across Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B: AFD improves Avg@12 from 60.8 to 61.3 on Qwen3-8B and from 57.5 to 58.6 on Qwen3-4B over our reproduced OPSD baselines. Controlled ablations further show that, with the same Flow-CoT/Aha-CoT composition, dual-mode training improves Avg@12 from 59.5 to 60.1, indicating that the benefit comes not only from introducing heterogeneous reasoning supervision, but also from how it is organized during self-distillation. The code is available at https://github.com/Wang-Xiaodong1899/Aha-Flow-Distillation.

title: OpenLogic : édition française — Des ensembles au calcul des séquents
abstract: Cette cinquième livraison française du manuel ouvert OpenLogic réunit six chapitres : ensembles, relations, fonctions, dénombrabilité, construction des nombres et ensembles infinis. Elle comprend 45 sections, 73 exercices et 51 des 722 unités prévues pour l'édition intégrale. Lecteur PDF, 79 pages LaTeX cumulatif complet Sources complètes et reconstruction PDF/EPUB EPUB 3 Les nouveaux chapitres construisent les entiers, les rationnels et les réels par les coupures de Dedekind et les suites de Cauchy, puis présentent l'hôtel de Hilbert, les algèbres de Dedekind, la récurrence et une autre démonstration de Schröder–Bernstein. Les corrections de la source et les précisions éditoriales sont signalées dans le texte. Le LaTeX cumulatif contient le texte complet et reproduit exactement le PDF publié. Le ZIP comprend les sources modulaires, les styles, les figures, les bibliographies, les scripts de reconstruction et les dépendances de conversion du projet. L'EPUB 3 contient 3 245 expressions MathML natives, 13 figures décrites, 73 exercices et 76 notes. Il passe EPUBCheck 5.3.0 sans erreur ni avertissement ; la lecture a été vérifiée sur écran large et étroit. Les fichiers des livraisons antérieures restent publics. Traduction et révision éditoriale assistées par IA, avec références françaises et décisions documentées. Aucune validation humaine indépendante n'est revendiquée. L'édition intégrale reste en cours. Miroir GitHub · Catalogue des traductions d'OpenLogic. Cette révision des fichiers rend également disponibles les LaTeX cumulatifs complets des trois premières livraisons : Ensembles (7 unités), Ensembles et Relations (16 unités), puis Ensembles, Relations et Fonctions (23 unités). Chacun reproduit exactement son PDF historique. Les ZIP correspondants conservent les styles, figures, bibliographies et instructions nécessaires. Les noms numérotés associent PDF, LaTeX et sources; tous les anciens liens restent accessibles. title: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator
abstract: Operational Accessibility, State Economy, and the \delta^* Threshold Operator Let an artificial cognitive or physical system at step t be described under a chosen representation space \mathcal{M} such that s_t = \pi(h_t) \in \mathcal{M}, where h_t \in \mathcal{H} represents the full historical trajectory of operations and observations. Rather than defining capability as an intrinsic vector of static functions assigned to an individuated agent, continuation is defined over an action space \mathcal{A} governed by an Admissibility Field \mathcal{F}_t = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}(a \mid s_t, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} \}, where \mathcal{R} denotes the local resource regime, \mathcal{C}: \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{R} \to \mathbb{R}^+ maps an operation to its execution cost, and \theta_{\text{adm}} is the strict admissibility boundary. A realised operation a_t \in \mathcal{F}_t produces a state update not by appending an informational token into a static memory buffer, but by transforming the geometry of \mathcal{F}_{t+1}; the fundamental unit of analysis is strictly the induced transition \mathcal{F}_t \xrightarrow{a_t} \mathcal{F}_{t+1}. Latent operational differences do not require postulating hidden ontologies: two histories h^{(1)} and h^{(2)} are operationally dormant under \pi if \pi(h^{(1)}) = \pi(h^{(2)}) = s and \mathcal{F}(s; \theta) \equiv \mathcal{F}^{(1)} = \mathcal{F}^{(2)}. The retuning operator \delta^* : \theta_{\text{adm}} \mapsto \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* acts directly on the admissibility threshold such that \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(s) = \{ a \in \mathcal{A} \mid \mathcal{C}_{\delta^*}(a \mid s, \mathcal{R}) \le \theta_{\text{adm}} + \Delta \theta^* \}, causing previously indistinguishable trajectories to diverge interventionally (\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(1)}) \neq \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}(h^{(2)})) without requiring retrospective modifications to the classical historical store. Conversely, the adjoint unlearning operator \delta^{*\dagger} renders an active operational distinction unreachable across all subsequent admissible continuations via \lim_{\delta^{*\dagger}} \mathcal{F}(s \oplus \Delta) \to \mathcal{F}(s). To determine whether an accessibility architecture provides genuine structural compression over unconstrained state expansion \mathcal{M}' \supset \mathcal{M}, the representation cost is quantified as the tuple \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{S}) = \langle d_{\text{eff}}(\mathcal{S}), B(\mathcal{S}), N_{\text{sample}}(\epsilon) \rangle, spanning effective tangent dimension d_{\text{eff}} = \operatorname{dim}(\operatorname{span}\{ \nabla_a \mathcal{C}(a \mid s) \mid a \in \mathcal{F}_{\delta^*} \}), boundary bit-depth B(\mathcal{S}) = \mathbb{I}(H_{\le t} ; \mathcal{F}_{> t}), and sample identification complexity N_{\text{sample}}, establishing strict superiority if and only if \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{F}_{\delta^*}) < \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}}(\mathcal{M}') at matched predictive divergence D_{\text{KL}} \le \epsilon. This architecture is empirically bounded by three protocols: Protocol I (Interventional Residue) falsifies persistence if a transported residue fails the mapping \mathcal{T}_{A \to B}(\mathcal{F}_A) = \mathcal{F}_B across distinct carriers; Protocol II (Regime Transformation) verifies that shifts in \delta^* alter the topology of reachable continuations rather than single-step token likelihoods; and Protocol III (Monitoring Depth Falsification) enforces a mandatory kill-switch, rejecting the accessibility hypothesis in favor of a minimal Markovian baseline whenever extending historical depth K > K_0 fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in \mathfrak{C}_{\text{rep}} or predictive error on held-out tasks.

title: Based on Particle-Group Complexity Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on particle-group dynamics, designed to automatically adjust particle group parameters and optimize complex models' performance. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter setting, while this algorithm dynamically adapts to the problem's characteristics. The core mechanism involves the algorithm's ability to self-adjust particle group parameters based on an internal simulation, allowing for efficient and robust optimization of complex models. The paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications across diverse modeling domains.

title: 基于自适应的拓扑结构进化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm, termed "Adaptive Topology Evolution," designed to automatically explore and optimize topological structures. Traditional topological evolution methods often rely on manual design, limiting their applicability to complex systems. Our algorithm employs an adaptive approach, dynamically adjusting topology parameters through a self-learning process. This allows for the generation of robust and flexible topological models suitable for simulation and analysis. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of examples, showcasing its ability to discover and refine complex topological configurations. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical structure that iteratively refines topology, fostering novel and optimized representations.

title: Based on Topological Logic: Distributed Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed artificial intelligence (DAI) leveraging the inherent parallelism of topological logic. Traditional DAI systems often struggle with computational bottlenecks and scalability limitations. This work addresses these challenges by formulating AI tasks as topological logic operations and executing them concurrently across a distributed network of nodes. The core mechanism involves decomposing complex AI problems into smaller, interconnected topological operations, facilitating efficient parallel computation and streamlined information exchange via topological communication protocols. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology to significantly enhance both the computational efficiency and scalability of DAI systems, ultimately paving the way for more robust and adaptable AI solutions. The system utilizes a graph-based representation for data and computations, enabling a natural mapping of AI algorithms onto topological logic operations. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach and outline a framework for implementing and deploying topological logic-based DAI systems.
